research_question: How do M1/M2 forward, backward, memory, and first-variation behavior scale over the declared control-side/batch/dtype/device matrix?

first_variation.projected_jvp_definition: reverse-mode scalar-alpha derivative of <cotangent,R(alpha)>; compared with <cotangent,d>

metric_definitions.canonical_redecode_error: Euclidean vertex error between D(E(Y)) and Y
metric_definitions.control_side: number of control vertices per square side; total vertices=control_side^2
metric_definitions.covariance_condition: largest/smallest eigenvalue of each 2x2 row covariance
metric_definitions.finite_difference_first_variation: central [R(+epsilon)-R(-epsilon)]/(2 epsilon) compared to requested full vertex tangent d
metric_definitions.gpu_memory: absolute PyTorch allocator peaks after warmup reset; reserved baseline includes cached warmup blocks
metric_definitions.projected_jvp: one deterministic dual projection of dR/dalpha computed by ordinary reverse-mode autograd; not a full forward-mode JVP
metric_definitions.solver_relative_residual: row Euclidean barycentric residual divided by max(norm(Y_i),norm(sum_j p_ij Y_j),tiny)
metric_definitions.timing: synchronized wall time; input cloning excluded; forward, scalar loss, and first-order reverse-mode backward reported separately
